item.text:
## 2B.4 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Bottom line: **mostly yes, with limits.** Kishida’s 2024 record is not a battlefield-command record, but in the conflicts Japan was addressing diplomatically, he consistently emphasized civilian protection, humanitarian access, hostage release, international law, and de-escalation. I found **no direct 2024 evidence** of Kishida endorsing unlawful prisoner abuse, indiscriminate force, or proportionality violations. The main limit is that Japan’s role was diplomatic and humanitarian, not operational.

### Supports
- **Summit on Peace in Ukraine (Summary)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html)  
  Kishida said peace in Ukraine must be “just and lasting,” grounded in the UN Charter and international law, and must not justify unilateral changes by force or coercion. He also said Japan would contribute to nuclear safety, electricity, and mine action. This is direct civilian-protection and necessity/proportionality evidence.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.9`

- **Signing of the Accord on Support for Ukraine and Cooperation between the Government of Japan and Ukraine (Summary)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 13, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/13accord.html)  
  The accord explicitly included security and defense, humanitarian support, and recovery/reconstruction, and said cooperation would be in accordance with Japan’s constitutional and legal requirements. That is evidence of a bounded, legality-conscious approach rather than open-ended militarization.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.7`

- **G7 Leaders’ statement on Gaza** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | June 4, 2024 | [link](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageite_000001_00384.html)  
  The G7 statement, which Japan joined, called for hostage release, humanitarian aid, protection of civilians, compliance with international law and international humanitarian law, and de-escalation. It also rejected attacks on civilians and threats to shipping. This is strong evidence of respect for civilian protection and humanitarian law.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`

- **On the Current Situation Surrounding the Gaza Strip** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | October 7, 2024 | [link](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00630.html)  
  Japan condemned the Hamas attacks, demanded hostage release, said the humanitarian situation in Gaza was critical, and urged all parties including Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and work toward ceasefire. This is direct evidence of civilian-protection and IHL language.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`

- **G7 Leaders’ Video Conference** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | April 15, 2024 | [link](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageit_000001_00279.html)  
  Kishida said Iran’s attack on Israel would further deteriorate the situation and stressed self-restraint to prevent further escalation. He also said Japan would work to protect and evacuate citizens. That is clear de-escalation and civilian-protection behavior in a crisis.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`

### Limits / Mixed
- **Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Seventy-Ninth Session of the United Nations General Assembly** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | September 28, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202409/0928enzetsu.html)  
  Kishida said Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and the dire situation in Palestine and Gaza required international cooperation grounded in the UN Charter and human dignity. This is still civilian-protection oriented, but it also shows Japan was endorsing continued political pressure and support for defensive war efforts, not purely humanitarian restraint.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `2B.1`

- **Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 6, 2024 | [link](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06hiroshima.html)  
  Kishida framed nuclear devastation as a moral lesson and reaffirmed non-use norms. This is relevant to civilian protection, but it is background normative framing rather than evidence from a live military operation.  
  Question IDs: `2B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`

### Gap
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** about Kishida handling prisoners of war, battlefield targeting choices, or operational proportionality decisions, because Japan was not conducting the relevant military operations.
- The available record is mainly **policy-level humanitarian and legal language**, which is still relevant, but it limits how far the judgment can go.
- Best reading: **yes on respect for civilian protection and humanitarian law in stated policy; no direct evidence of battlefield violations or prisoner-abuse decisions.**
